Despite Trump’s Promises To Lower Prices, Americans Are Still Asking, ‘Where’s The Beef?’

‘There’s a lot of frustration and anger’

Actual Article Body:
(Photo by Kent NISHIMURA / AFP via Getty Images)

President Donald Trump’s moves to allow foreign beef to flood domestic markets in an attempt to lower prices may have been a losing bet.

Trump is still facing backlash from U.S. ranchers and some Republicans over his decision to allow the importing of roughly 600 million pounds of foreign-supplied beef, POLITICO reported Friday. The move comes after beef prices rose to $6.92 per pound in August, up from the January 2025 average of $5.55 per pound. (RELATED: Ranchers Say Beef Market Has ‘Been Hell’ As Trump Announces Plan To Try And Help)

“President Trump has done more for American agriculture than anyone by negotiating new trade deals, expanding foreign market access, lowering input costs, bolstering the farm safety net, doubling the death tax exemption, ending taxes on rural property loan interest, creating rural opportunity zones, and more,” White House spokeswoman Anna Kelly told the Daily Caller News Foundation. “At the same time, he is delivering on his promise to consumers by reducing beef prices while allowing our American beef herd to grow. The President will continue taking actions to support our great farmers while driving economic prosperity for all Americans.”

The U.S. Department of Agriculture did not immediately respond to the DCNF’s request for comment.

“There’s a lot of frustration and anger,” Kansas Farm Bureau President Glenn Brunkow, a fifth-generation farmer, told the outlet.

Brunkow said opening beef imports to countries like Brazil reduces the value of the American cow — which can usually sell for roughly $2,000 — by $200 to $400.

“We knew it wouldn’t have much of an effect on the hamburger price in the store. But the markets took that news, and it really knocked the price we get for our cattle down,” he said.

Republican Wyoming Sen. Cynthia Lummis likewise told POLITICO she’s still facing backlash from ranchers in her state over the Trump’s “somewhat self-defeating” proclamation.

Lummis, however, isn’t the only Republican lawmaker to criticize the gambit.

Shortly after Trump — who famously campaigned for protectionist policies — posted Aug. 21 to Truth Social that the U.S. “will allow up to 300,000 metric tons of product for ground beef to be imported with no out of quota tariff [for the next 90 days]” and sell the beef “25 percent below current market prices,” Republican Sens. Chuck Grassley of Iowa and Tim Sheehy of Montana voiced their concerns on X.

Grassley posted he was “concerned for the cattle markets” and that the White House should instead focus on fighting the screwworm epidemic threatening the health of U.S. cattle while expanding domestic herds.

After Tyson closure in Illinois last wk I’m concerned for the cattle markets +now Pres Trump’s decision to temporarily open up subsidized beef imports USA cattlemen shld always be put 1st thru America 1st policies Need 2keep up progress fighting screwworm+ expanding domestic herd

“I’ve advised President Trump against this course of action for a year because American ranchers have been struggling against the packer monopoly for decades, and this will further harm them - most of whom are MAGA Republicans,” Sheehy also posted that same day.

I’ve advised President Trump against this course of action for a year because American ranchers have been struggling against the packer monopoly for decades, and this will further harm them - most of whom are MAGA Republicans. The President’s heart is in the right place on wanting lower prices for the American people, and beef prices have been impacted by the Mexican screwworm. But the reality is this action will make it more difficult for American ranchers to rebuild our herd and bring prices down for the American people. And most importantly, this will harm our ranching families who feed the nation.

Causing no discernible effect on prices, an estimated 8,054 to 21,936 metric tons of beef were imported into the U.S. in September that otherwise would not have entered the domestic market, the University of Arkansas reported.

The DCNF also reached out to Sens. Lummis, Grassley, Sheehy, and Jerry Moran of Kansas, along with the National Cattlemen’s Beef Association, the American Farm Bureau Federation, the U.S. Cattlemen’s Association, the Montana Cattlemen’s Association, the Montana Farmers Union, and the Kansas Farm Bureau for comments.

Editor’s note: This report was updated with a comment from the White House.

Trump says he'd 'love' to have Sen. John Fetterman as a Republican amid growing speculation

President Donald Trump called Sen. John Fetterman a "great guy" and said he would welcome the Pennsylvania Democrat into the Republican Party ranks.

Actual Article Body:

President Donald Trump praised Sen. John Fetterman, D-Pa., as a "great guy" with "great common sense," saying he would welcome the Pennsylvania Democrat into the Republican Party.

President Donald Trump praised Sen. John Fetterman, D-Pa., as a "great guy" on Saturday, saying he would welcome the Pennsylvania Democrat into the Republican Party.

Trump was asked by a reporter after stepping off Air Force One at Joint Base Andrews whether he had spoken to Fetterman — who has repeatedly broken with Democrats during the current session of Congress — about becoming a Republican and whether he would welcome such a switch.

"I'd love to see it. I think he's great," Trump responded.

"It's going to be hard for him to get the nomination as a Democrat, but I'd love to have him as a Republican," he continued.

REPUBLICANS SAY THEY'D WELCOME FETTERMAN AS GOP EYES BIGGER SENATE MAJORITY

President Donald Trump said he would welcome Democratic Sen. John Fetterman into the Republican Party, praising the Pennsylvania lawmaker's judgment and common sense. (Aaron Schwartz/Getty Images)

Trump described Fetterman as a "great guy" with "magnificent parents," whom he said he had spoken with previously.

"He's a very solid person," Trump added. "He's smart and all that, but he's got great common sense."

Trump also suggested that switching parties could benefit Fetterman politically.

"If you look at the polls, he does better as a Republican than he does as a Democrat," he said.

MAVERICK DEMOCRAT SURGES WITH REPUBLICANS AS HIS OWN PARTY TURNS ON HIM, STOKING TALK OF GOP SWITCH

Sen. John Fetterman, D-Pa., speaks to reporters following a briefing by Trump administration officials to members of the Senate on U.S. strikes on Iran, at the U.S. Capitol in Washington, D.C. on March 3, 2026. (Sen. John Fetterman)

Trump's comments come as Fetterman has repeatedly broken with Democrats on key issues, including the Iran war and immigration, although he continues to vote with his party the vast majority of the time.

Since joining the Senate in 2023, Fetterman has voted with Senate Democrats nearly 90% of the time. During the current session of Congress, however, that figure has fallen to just under 81%, Fox News Digital previously reported.

Fetterman's occasional breaks with his party have fueled speculation in recent months about whether he might eventually become a Republican. He has also reportedly used Republican fundraising platforms to solicit donations and maintains a close friendship with Sen. Katie Britt, R-Ala.

Last month, Fetterman recorded a video introducing Sen. Dave McCormick, R-Pa., at the Republican Midterm Convention.

FETTERMAN TEASES WHERE HIS TRUE LOYALTY LIES AFTER SURPRISE APPEARANCE AT GOP CONVENTION

Sen. John Fetterman, D-Pa., has broken with fellow Democrats on several high-profile issues, prompting speculation about his political future. (Andrew Harnik/Getty Images)

He also mistakenly referred to himself as a lifelong Republican during an appearance at the Texas Tribune's TribFest last month.

An attendee at the event asked why Fetterman did not run as an independent.

"Because I'm a lifelong Republican," he said, before realizing his mistake. "I guarantee you that will break through. That will get clipped."

Fox News Digital has reached out to Fetterman's office for comment.

Donald Trump Laments Not Receiving Nobel Peace Prize: 'Settled 8 Wars'

President Donald Trump lamented in a social media post that he and the United States were not awarded the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize.
The post Donald Trump Laments Not Receiving Nobel Peace Prize: ‘Settled 8 Wars’ appeared first on Breitbart.

Actual Article Body:
President Donald Trump lamented that he and the United States did not receive the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize, and pointed out that he has “settled 8 wars” and is also “close to ending or settling 2 more.”

In a post on Truth Social, Trump also highlighted how he and his administration helped get “all of the Israeli hostages back” and how his administration “captured the violent dictator” of Venezuela. Trump’s post comes after it was revealed that Navanethem “Navi” Pillay, a South African judge and former United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights, had received the Nobel Peace Prize.

“I settled 8 WARS, am close to ending or settling 2 more, got all of the Israeli hostages back, including the final 28, both living and dead, had hundreds of hostages, from countries all over the World, released and sent back home, won a war in Venezuela, and captured the violent dictator who so viciously ran that country, and stopped the number one state sponsor of terror, the Islamic Republic of Iran, from obtaining a Nuclear Weapon — AND MUCH MORE! Yet, with all of that I, or the United States of America, did not get the Noble Peace Prize. WOW!” Trump wrote.

Breitbart News’s John Hayward reported that some criticized the choice, calling it “purely political”:

Critics blasted the award as a purely political move intended to “send a message” to President Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, since Pillay has denounced Israel for “genocide” in Gaza without corresponding criticism of the October 7 atrocities or the terrorists of Hamas.

If the Nobel committee was trying to infuriate the Israelis by giving the Peace Prize to a “Gaza genocide” activist just two days after the anniversary of the 10/7 attack, it succeeded.

In a statement the Israeli Foreign Ministry said, “If there were an award for lies, hatred, and blood libels, Navi Pillay wouldn’t just be a contender,” she would “be a frontrunner.”

Pillay, who is also “currently serving as an ad hoc judge at the International Court of Justice (ICJ)” was also criticized in a statement from Netanyahu’s office.

“Navi Pillay’s proudest achievement was to legitimize a corrupt prosecutor who turned to her fabrications against Israel hoping that by joining her bigoted lynch mob, he would beat a rape charge,” the statement from Netanyahu’s office said.

Breitbart News reported that María Corina Machado, who received the Nobel Peace Prize in 2025, “dedicated her recognition” not only to the Venezuelan people, but also to Donald Trump.

“We are on the threshold of victory and today, more than ever, we count on President Trump, the people of the United States, the peoples of Latin America, and the democratic nations of the world,” Machado said at the time.

“I dedicate this prize to the suffering people of Venezuela and to President Trump for his decisive support of our cause!” she added.
